overview: The Medford City Council met to organize for the 2017 term, electing new leadership and adopting council rules. The Council also received an update on the Hallmark Health merger, voted to accept state provisions lowering default speed limits to 25 mph, referred a zoning resolution to committee, and approved final funding for Riverside Plaza.

items.title: Election of Council President for 2017
items.summary: The Council elected Councilor Richard F. Caraviello as City Council President for 2017, after which he took the oath of office.

items.title: Election of Council Vice President for 2017
items.summary: The Council elected Councilor Michael Marks as City Council Vice President for 2017, after which he took the oath of office.

items.title: Adoption of Standing Committee Rules
items.summary: The Council voted to adopt the standing committee rules as the Council rules for 2017.

items.title: Transfer of Papers from 2016 Council
items.summary: The Council approved transferring all pending committee papers from the 2016 Council to the 2017 Council.

items.title: Common Victualler License for Compass Group / Eurest Dining Services
items.summary: The Council approved a common victualler license petition for Compass Group doing business as Eurest Dining Services at 20 Cabot Road.

items.title: Hallmark Health Merger Presentation
items.summary: Hallmark Health System President Alan McDonald briefed the Council on Hallmark's partnership with Tufts Medical Center and Lowell General Hospital under Wellforce, addressing questions regarding governance, clinical services, and capital investments.

items.title: Resolution on Default Speed Limits and Pedestrian Safety Zones
items.summary: The Council voted to accept statutory provisions allowing the city to reduce default speed limits to 25 mph and referred pedestrian safety zone designations, equipment upgrades, and staffing requests to the Traffic Commission and administration.

items.title: Resolution on Prohibiting Use Variances
items.summary: The Council referred a resolution opposing use variances to the Committee of the Whole to discuss comprehensive zoning policy with the administration, while requesting 20 years of variance records from the building commissioner.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: The Council expressed condolences to the families of Navy veteran Nicholas DeMaria and 105-year-old resident Mary Cecchini.

items.title: Business Under Suspension and Commendations
items.summary: A resident commended DPW water crews for emergency Christmas Eve main repairs, the Council voted to seek feedback from the Chamber of Commerce regarding potential plastic bag restrictions, and approved a resolution honoring State Representative Paul Donato's 16 years of service.

items.title: Third Reading of Riverside Plaza Reconstruction Funding
items.summary: The Council approved on third reading a $250,000 grant acceptance and $550,000 appropriation for the reconstruction of Riverside Plaza.
